text.arabic_uthmani: فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَآئِمُونَ

words.gloss_range: result and sequence particle binding this ayah to the prior oath failure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the completed circling visitation verb governed by the opening particle

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) makes the visitation a consequence, not a loose next scene. It binds the completed event of {{ar:طَافَ}} ({{tr:ṭāfa}}) directly to the prior failure to make exception in 68:18, so the ayah opens as immediate answer and narrative pivot. Even the bound spelling keeps the connector fused to the event verb, while the short onset releases into the heavier circling action.

topics.headline: immediate consequence of the failed exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the destructive visitation is presented as the direct next consequence of the oath failure in 68:18, not as an isolated episode.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a result/sequence particle, and the local main clause begins immediately with the perfect event verb.

topics.headline: connector fused to the event verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees how the first word pivots from the owners' plan into the counter-action by attaching the consequence marker directly to the action.
topics.reason: The particle is proclitic on {{ar:طَافَ}} ({{tr:ṭāfa}}), so the structural turn and the completed action arrive together.

topics.headline: light onset into heavy action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the quick connector give way to the heavier onset of the circling verb, matching the sudden narrative turn.
topics.reason: The phonetic row supports an audible transition without changing the grammar.

words.gloss_range: completed Form I circling or visitation against a target through {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}})
words.root_gloss_range: circling, going around, visitation, patrolling, and overwhelming encompassment; devotional and flood-like branches are background contrasts, not the local sense by themselves

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the prepositional target surface governed by the circling verb
the cognate active-participle subject that performs the visitation

words.prose: {{ar:طَافَ}} ({{tr:ṭāfa}}) presents the counter-action as a completed Form I visitation. The verb is intransitive and reaches the garden through {{ar:عَلَيْهَا}} ({{tr:ʿalayhā}}), so the garden is a target surface over which the motion passes, not a direct object or companion. Its {{ar:ط و ف}} ({{tr:ṭ-w-f}}) field gives the action a circling, encompassing, patrol-like feel, while Form I keeps it direct rather than causative or intensive. The repeated root with {{ar:طَآئِفٌ}} ({{tr:ṭāʾifun}}) makes act and actor echo each other; the long vowel and emphatic onset let that circuit sound heavy as well as semantic. The same visitation-source frame has a 7:201 contrast with a satanic source, while here the later sleep clause belongs to this main action as its circumstance.

topics.headline: completed circling upon a target surface
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a completed hostile pass over the garden, not a vague strike or an ongoing warning.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect Form I and intransitive with a forced {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) complement.

topics.headline: circling field narrowed to punitive visitation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the event as encompassing traversal of the garden, while devotional or flood branches remain contextual contrasts rather than direct translation choices.
topics.reason: V4 preserves circling, overwhelming event, visitation, and patrol branches, but the local Form I plus {{ar:عَلَيْهَا}} ({{tr:ʿalayhā}}) narrows the active payoff to punitive circling visitation.

topics.headline: Form I avoids intensive or causative coloring
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the motion is assigned directly to the visitor, without presenting repeated rounds, self-directed devotion, or an external causer as the wording's focus.
topics.reason: The local surface is Form I perfect, so nearby Form II, reflexive, or causative family possibilities can only clarify what is not being foregrounded.

topics.headline: verb and visitor echo one root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the act and actor mutually reinforce each other: a circling visitation is performed by a circling visitor.
topics.reason: {{ar:طَافَ}} ({{tr:ṭāfa}}) and {{ar:طَآئِفٌ}} ({{tr:ṭāʾifun}}) share the same root in adjacent action and subject slots.

topics.headline: visitation frame contrasted by source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a visitation frame also appears with a satanic source in 7:201, while this ayah defines the source as the addressee's Lord.
topics.reason: The 7:201 parallel can illuminate source contrast, but it does not control the local parse or make the local visitor demonic.

topics.headline: main action governs the sleep circumstance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the owners' sleep as the circumstance of the visitation, sharpening the contrast between active intervention and human passivity.
topics.reason: The nominal sleep clause is marked as a circumstantial clause attached to the main verb.

topics.headline: heavy repeated circling sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the repeated long vowel and emphatic onset reinforce the weight of the circling action.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows track the shared root sound across verb and subject.

words.gloss_range: preposition {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) with feminine suffix, marking the garden as the surface and target of the visitation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the circling verb that governs the prepositional target phrase
the masculine plural pronoun for the sleeping owners

words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهَا}} ({{tr:ʿalayhā}}) keeps the garden in the ayah through a compressed feminine suffix. The preposition is governed by {{ar:طَافَ}} ({{tr:ṭāfa}}), so the garden is the surface upon which the visitation moves and the target against which it bears, while the noun itself remains unnamed. This also separates the pronoun track for the garden from the later {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) for the sleeping owners.

topics.headline: feminine suffix resumes the garden
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the garden remains the target without being renamed, carried forward by a feminine suffix from 68:17.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence strongly links the suffix to the earlier garden.

topics.headline: uponness becomes hostile coverage
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the garden not merely as a location but as the surface covered by a hostile circling pass.
topics.reason: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) is the forced complement of the intransitive verb and marks the garden as target surface.

topics.headline: garden and owners remain distinct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that property and people are kept on separate pronoun tracks: the garden receives the visitation while the owners sleep.
topics.reason: The feminine suffix and masculine plural pronoun have different antecedents in the attachment evidence.

words.gloss_range: indefinite masculine singular active participle, the circling visitor or visitation that acts as subject
words.root_gloss_range: circler, visitor, apparition, affliction, patrol, and bounded portion; local form keeps singular agentive visitation primary

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the cognate verb mirrored by the active-participle subject
the feminine collective derivative contrasted with the local masculine singular participle
the variant specter-form contrasted with the local canonical active participle
the source phrase that fixes the visitor's provenance

words.prose: {{ar:طَآئِفٌ}} ({{tr:ṭāʾifun}}) names the subject only after the garden has already been exposed. Its masculine singular active participle makes the actor a singular visitor or visitation, not the feminine collective {{ar:طَائِفَة}} ({{tr:ṭāʾifa}}). Tanwīn leaves the instrument unidentified, while {{ar:مِنْ رَبِّكَ}} ({{tr:min rabbika}}) fixes its provenance. The same source-frame has a 7:201 contrast with an opposed source, so provenance is part of the payoff, not a generic origin label. The variant pressure of {{ar:طَيْفٌ}} ({{tr:ṭayfun}}) sharpens the sense of an elusive, apparition-like visitation, but the local canonical form remains the agentive circler that mirrors {{ar:طَافَ}} ({{tr:ṭāfa}}). Its marked participial slot and hamza catch make the visitor distinctive in sound and form, not merely indefinite.

topics.headline: singular participial subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the actor is a singular agentive visitation, not a human group or abstract process.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify a masculine singular active participle serving as the nominative subject of {{ar:طَافَ}} ({{tr:ṭāfa}}).

topics.headline: source known, instrument unnamed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the ayah identifies where the visitor is from while withholding what exactly the instrument is.
topics.reason: The subject remains indefinite, and the following source phrase restricts origin without making the agent definite.

topics.headline: circler, visitor, affliction, apparition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the visitor as mobile and elusive, while the wording still avoids naming wind, fire, frost, angel, or any other specific instrument.
topics.reason: The accepted root branches include circling, visitation, apparition, and affliction, but the local form and source phrase keep the instrument unspecified.

topics.headline: variant specter pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can register an accepted variant's apparition-like coloring without replacing the canonical participial circler.
topics.reason: The variant {{ar:طَيْفٌ}} ({{tr:ṭayfun}}) is useful contrast, but the aligned local surface is {{ar:طَآئِفٌ}} ({{tr:ṭāʾifun}}).

topics.headline: portion and group field kept secondary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader avoids turning the word into a human party or section; any portion-pressure stays secondary under the singular participle.
topics.reason: The feminine collective or portion noun field is real in the root family, but the local masculine singular participle blocks making it primary.

topics.headline: same visitation frame, opposed source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase pattern has a 7:201 counterpart with a satanic source, making this ayah's divine provenance more pointed.
topics.reason: The 7:201 echo clarifies source contrast, not local identity.

topics.headline: actor mirrors its action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the subject as etymologically fitted to its own action, intensifying the compactness of the visitation clause.
topics.reason: The verb and subject share {{ar:ط و ف}} ({{tr:ṭ-w-f}}) in adjacent slots.

topics.headline: marked participle with audible catch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and notices the marked participial form as a distinctive way to characterize the visitor.
topics.reason: The active participle is distributionally marked in the supplied profiles, and the sound row coheres with that surface.

words.gloss_range: source preposition governing {{ar:رَبِّكَ}} ({{tr:rabbika}}), with secondary partitive or classificatory pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the visitor modified by the source prepositional phrase
the genitive source noun governed by the preposition

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) makes provenance explicit before the owners' sleep is mentioned. It governs {{ar:رَبِّكَ}} ({{tr:rabbika}}) and most tightly modifies {{ar:طَآئِفٌ}} ({{tr:ṭāʾifun}}): the visitor is from the addressee's Lord. Its partitive and classificatory possibilities remain secondary pressures, suggesting limited allotment or domain, but the local syntax first marks source rather than explaining the material instrument. The same visitation-source template is visible by contrast in 7:201, where the source noun changes.

topics.headline: source phrase for the visitor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah identifies the visitor's authority and origin before identifying what happened to the owners.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:رَبِّكَ}} ({{tr:rabbika}}) the genitive complement of {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) modifying the visitor as source.

topics.headline: source belongs before the sleep clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the source phrase as part of the visitation complex, not as a description of the owners' sleeping.
topics.reason: The phrase is completed inside the main verbal event before the circumstantial sleep clause begins.

topics.headline: secondary portion or domain shading
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear a limited allotment or domain nuance without losing the primary source relation.
topics.reason: The preposition can carry partitive or classifying force, but attachment evidence favors source provenance locally.

topics.headline: visitation-source formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same source-frame pattern as 7:201, with the source noun changed in this ayah.
topics.reason: The intertext row supplies a concrete 7:201 comparison, useful for source substitution rather than local semantic replacement.

words.gloss_range: the addressee's Lord as genitive source of the visitation
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, ownership, governance, sustaining, nurture, cultivation, and related extended branches; local sense centers on divine lordship and source authority

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the second-person masculine singular suffix embedded in the source title

words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّكَ}} ({{tr:rabbika}}) brings divine source into the parable as a governed genitive noun, not as a finite verb. The suffix {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:-ka}}) turns the third-person garden story toward the addressee: the visitor is from your Lord. The root's lordship and nurturing range matters because the target is a garden; the source of cultivation and governance is also the source of the undoing. The same addressee-Lord formula participates in decisive intervention contexts such as 89:13 and 69:11, and the visitation-source frame contrasts with 7:201 by changing the source. The phrase stands between the visitation and the sleeping clause, placing provenance before human oblivion.

topics.headline: lordship as governed source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Lord is named as source by title and relation while the operative instrument remains unnamed.
topics.reason: {{ar:رَبِّكَ}} ({{tr:rabbika}}) is genitive under {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}), so it marks provenance rather than functioning as the clause's finite actor.

topics.headline: your Lord inside the story
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the parable briefly turns toward the addressed listener by saying your Lord inside an otherwise third-person scene.
topics.reason: The second-person suffix is attached to the source noun and is licensed as the singular addressee marker.

topics.headline: definite without article
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the source is not an unnamed lord but the definite Lord of the addressee, carried by attachment rather than an article.
topics.reason: The possessive suffix creates definiteness and direct-address force inside the noun.

topics.headline: cultivator-source reverses garden nurture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pointed reversal: the Lord associated with governance, sustaining, and cultivation is the source of the visitation against a cultivated garden.
topics.reason: V4 supports lordship, authority, repair, nurture, and completion branches, but the local noun title centers these as divine source authority in the garden parable.

topics.headline: lordship thread in punitive intervention
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect this source formula to other decisive intervention contexts, including 89:13 and 69:11, without making that formula exhaust the local meaning.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete punishment-context parallels and same-surah recurrence, but the local syntax still supplies the controlling source phrase.

topics.headline: provenance before oblivion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees divine provenance placed between the destructive action and the owners' unawareness.
topics.reason: The source phrase closes the main event complex before the circumstantial sleep clause.

topics.headline: source noun changes the visitation frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same visitation-source pattern can be reversed by source identity, as in the contrast with 7:201.
topics.reason: The concrete 7:201 parallel is a source contrast and does not alter the local divine provenance.

words.gloss_range: circumstantial connector opening the while-they-were-asleep clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the main event verb to which the circumstantial clause attaches
the nominal circumstantial clause naming the owners' sleep-state

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa-}}) opens the final clause as circumstance, not as a second equal event. It routes {{ar:هُمْ نَآئِمُونَ}} ({{tr:hum nāʾimūna}}) back to {{ar:طَافَ}} ({{tr:ṭāfa}}), so the owners' sleep is simultaneous with the visitation. The connector also delays the owners' state until after source has been named, creating the irony that the audience knows what the sleepers do not. The closing movement softens through muted nasal sounds, making the sleep-state audible rather than merely stated.

topics.headline: while, not simple and
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands the sleep clause as simultaneous circumstance during the visitation, not a separate later action.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following nominal clause as the circumstantial clause attached to the main verb.

topics.headline: sleep attaches to the action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the owners' state defines the conditions of the action, not the Lord or a coordinated event.
topics.reason: The connector points the final nominal clause back to {{ar:طَافَ}} ({{tr:ṭāfa}}), not to {{ar:رَبِّكَ}} ({{tr:rabbika}}).

topics.headline: detached pronoun completes the hal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the single-letter connector needs the following pronoun to form a full nominal circumstance.
topics.reason: The final clause is nominal, with {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) as subject and {{ar:نَآئِمُونَ}} ({{tr:nāʾimūna}}) as predicate.

topics.headline: audience knows before sleepers do
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the irony that the visitation has been sourced and narrated while the owners remain unaware.
topics.reason: The final state is introduced after the source phrase, making unawareness part of the scene's closure.

topics.headline: muted nasal close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the closing state soften into nasal sounds suited to sleep.
topics.reason: The phonetic row supports the auditory texture of the final clause without changing the syntax.

words.gloss_range: detached masculine plural pronoun subject of the nominal circumstantial clause
words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) gives the sleep clause its own explicit subject. The masculine plural pronoun resumes the garden owners from 68:17-18, excluding the feminine garden and the singular visitor. It turns the prior planners into the current sleepers as one collective group, and the detached form lets the final clause stand as a compact nominal state rather than a suffixal afterthought.

topics.headline: explicit subject of the sleep clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the owners' sleep stated as a full nominal circumstance with its own subject.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) as the subject of the nominal clause whose predicate is {{ar:نَآئِمُونَ}} ({{tr:nāʾimūna}}).

topics.headline: same planners are now asleep
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sleepers are the same garden owners whose oath and plan set up the consequence in 68:17-18.
topics.reason: The pronoun antecedent is strongly licensed as the plural garden owners.

topics.headline: not garden, not visitor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader avoids confusing the sleepers with the garden or the visitor because agreement separates the referents.
topics.reason: The masculine plural pronoun cannot resume the feminine garden, and the predicate agreement points to the plural owners.

topics.headline: whole group under one state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the whole owner group gathered under one state of unawareness, with no vigilant exception foregrounded.
topics.reason: The pronoun and predicate are masculine plural, assigning the state collectively.

topics.headline: independent pronoun opens the final state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final state is given a compact clause rather than being appended as a mere modifier.
topics.reason: The detached pronoun supplies the subject slot required for the nominal circumstantial clause.

words.gloss_range: masculine plural active participle predicate naming the owners' ongoing sleep-state
words.root_gloss_range: sleep, repose, suspended awareness, heedless quiet, and death-adjacent stillness; local form names literal sleeping persons with moral and vulnerability pressure
words.prose: {{ar:نَآئِمُونَ}} ({{tr:nāʾimūna}}) closes the ayah with the owners' state rather than with the visible result. As a masculine plural active participle, it predicates ongoing sleep of the whole group during the visitation, not a separate completed act of sleeping and not the visitor's state. The root field supports suspended awareness and heedless quiet, so the literal sleep also exposes moral inattention, but dream, causative sleep, and full death readings stay secondary. Sleep in sudden-danger contexts such as 7:97 sharpens the vulnerability: their earlier night planning is answered while they cannot perceive or control the outcome. The participial form is marked in the supplied sleep field, and its plural nasal ending helps round off the ayah. The result waits for 68:20, while 68:19 ends on human unawareness after divine action.

topics.headline: ongoing sleep predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that sleep is the owners' ongoing state during the visitation, not a new narrated action.
topics.reason: The word is an active participle predicate in a nominal circumstantial clause.

topics.headline: plural predicate belongs to the owners
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the sleeping state belongs to the owners collectively, not to the singular visitor.
topics.reason: The masculine plural nominative predicate agrees with {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) and not with singular {{ar:طَآئِفٌ}} ({{tr:ṭāʾifun}}).

topics.headline: literal sleep carrying heedlessness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader registers literal bodily sleep as also characterizing suspended awareness and moral inattention.
topics.reason: V4 supports sleep and heedless quiet branches, but the local active participle names sleeping persons first.

topics.headline: dream, causative sleep, and death kept secondary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader avoids overreading the word as a dream scene, a statement that they were put to sleep, or literal death, while still sensing death-adjacent loss of control.
topics.reason: The local surface is an active sleeper participle; broader dream, causative, and death branches can color vulnerability but do not replace the local sense.

topics.headline: sleep as exposed unawareness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees sleep as the condition under which the counter-action unfolds, making the owners vulnerable rather than merely resting.
topics.reason: The final sleep state is simultaneous with the visitation and appears in a punishment-risk scene; 7:97 is a useful pattern reference.

topics.headline: ayah closes on passive state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah move from active visitation to human passivity, ending with condition rather than aftermath.
topics.reason: The final nominal clause is structurally complete and closes the ayah on the owners' state.

topics.headline: night planning answered in sleep
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that the night setting of human planning becomes the setting of their inability to control the outcome.
topics.reason: The boundary rows link the prior night-oriented plan in 68:17-18 to the sleeping closure in 68:19.

topics.headline: result waits for the next ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 68:19 stops with unawareness and delays the visible garden aftermath until 68:20.
topics.reason: The row supplies the concrete next-ayah reference, so the topic is useful as a boundary observation.

topics.headline: marked participle and nasal ending
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final word as a marked form whose plural nasal ending helps round off the clause.
topics.reason: The supplied profiles mark the local form as uncommon, and the sound row concerns the final nasal closure.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The cognate doubling of the verb and agent noun at words 1 and 3, joined to عليها, makes the passage itself the focus ayah's dominant figure.
baseline_models.mechanism: The same root supplies motion around a target, an encompassing event, and an incident that comes upon it. The repetition therefore lets the event be both movement and mover: a bounded visitation closes around the feminine target while the humans are unavailable in sleep.

activation_trace.role: Literal circling supplies the event's trajectory and makes عليها a spatial center rather than merely an affected object.
The encompassing flood, darkness, or event turns a single pass into total coverage of the target.
The visiting incident gives the repeated agent noun event-like agency: something comes upon and closely visits the target.
Literal sleep fixes the human participants in an interval during which the encompassing motion proceeds without response.

changed_reading.before: An unspecified thing passed over the feminine target while some people slept.
changed_reading.after: A self-presenting visitation circles and envelops the target, acquiring agency from the verb-agent cognate repetition while the sleepers cannot interrupt it.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The night-patrol branch of طائف stands directly against the plural sleepers at word 7 and is marked as coming from the addressee's Rabb.
baseline_models.mechanism: A patrol normally preserves what it circles. Here the only active watcher is the visitation from the Rabb, while the humans have settled into sleep and trust. The ayah can therefore stage a transfer of custody: human surveillance is offline, and a higher authority patrols the target for an opposed purpose.

activation_trace.role: The literal night watchman supplies a patrol function, here inverted from protective custody into adverse inspection.
Settling trust explains sleep functionally as surrendered vigilance, not only a biological state.
Lordship, ownership, and authority identify the patrol's superior source and displace any assumed human control of the target.

changed_reading.before: The disaster happens opportunistically because the humans happen to be asleep.
changed_reading.after: Sleep marks a custody reversal: the human keepers withdraw into trust while an authoritative counter-watch circles what they presumed to control.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The source phrase من ربك makes origin part of the event's description, while the visiting-incident branch keeps the action anchored in طاف/طائف.
baseline_models.mechanism: The Rabb branch includes stage-by-stage tending, repair, completion, and administration. Coupled with a visitation that comes upon the target and with the sleepers' heedless obscurity, this permits an administrative reading: locally destructive action can still be corrective ordering rather than an ownerless accident.

activation_trace.role: Repair, nurture, completion, and administration supply a corrective purpose to the event's stated origin.
The incident that comes upon a target provides the concrete intervention through which administration is enacted.
Heedless quiet and social obscurity make the sleepers' non-recognition the condition against which corrective intervention operates.

changed_reading.before: The phrase from your Rabb only assigns the calamity's source.
changed_reading.after: The source phrase also opens a model of corrective administration: the visitation reorders a target whose human custodians remain heedlessly inactive.

context_deltas.mechanism: Context first activates concealment and then resolves the feminine target as a garden whose lexical image is vegetation-screened enclosure. The encompassing pass in the focus ayah consequently reads as a perimeter event that defeats the very screened boundedness by which the garden is recognizable.

activation_trace.role: The encompassing event supplies total pressure around and over the still-unresolved feminine target.
The concealment image primes hiddenness as a live property of the context before the garden episode begins.
The tree-screened garden resolves عليها and gives the focus event a vegetatively enclosed spatial object to breach.

structural_cues: The feminine pronoun عليها in 68:19 receives its immediate antecedent from the garden in 68:17.
The same concealment root occurs before the garden narrative and inside its opening designation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a concealed garden and an encompassing event; I infer that the enclosure is functionally breached. A live weaker alternative is that context only identifies the target without making concealment part of the event's mechanism.

changed_reading.before: An encompassing incident affects an unidentified feminine target.
changed_reading.after: The incident closes around and penetrates a tree-screened enclosure, making the garden's apparent privacy precisely what fails.

context_deltas.mechanism: The wider sequence names withholding good, then has the owners police entry against a poor person, and finally has them call themselves deprived. The focus event's encircling-wall image can therefore act on the social boundary itself: the exclusionary perimeter rebounds, barring the would-be gatekeepers from the yield they meant to monopolize.

activation_trace.role: The encircling wall supplies a boundary image that can carry the episode's contested access relation.
Withholding the hand from giving supplies the social function later instantiated by the owners' plan.
Literal entry locates the owners' policy at the garden boundary and makes access, not only fruit, part of the mechanism.
The abasement of poverty identifies the person whom the planned boundary is designed to keep outside.
Deprivation and loss of the sought object turn exclusion back upon the intending excluders.

structural_cues: The owners whisper an explicit no-entry policy in 68:24 after the focus event but before seeing its result.
Their self-description in 68:27 reverses the direction of deprivation without changing its basic access logic.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies withholding, denied entry, an encircling boundary, and the owners' deprivation; I supply the reciprocal arrow by which the boundary policy rebounds on its makers. The event could alternatively destroy the crop without symbolically executing the access policy.

changed_reading.before: The passing event destroys private produce.
changed_reading.after: The event judges a private boundary: those who planned to keep need outside are themselves enclosed outside the benefit they claimed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The narrative labels the episode an assay whose function is to make a condition appear, surrounds the focus with planned cutting and the cut-off result, and times disclosure for morning. The visiting incident becomes the instrument that severs continuity during sleep so that an inward disposition becomes externally legible at dawn.

activation_trace.role: Corrective administration supplies a possible purpose for an intervention that is destructive at the local level.
The visiting incident is the concrete mediator between concealed intention and visible result.
Testing that makes a state appear assigns revelatory function to the whole garden sequence.
Cutting and separation provide the intended human operation that the event preempts and redirects.
The night/day cut-off image makes the result both material severance and a temporal threshold.
First light supplies the scheduled disclosure point against which the sleepers' interval is measured.

structural_cues: The focus ayah is placed between the owners' oath to cut in the morning and the garden's morning transformation.
The clause وهم نائمون makes non-observation the hinge between intention and revealed condition.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an assay, severance language, sleep, and dawn disclosure; I infer that the passing event is the assay's operative instrument. The live alternative is that testing characterizes the episode as a whole while the event remains only its calamity.

changed_reading.before: The event is an unexplained nocturnal calamity.
changed_reading.after: It is a timed assay by severance: concealed intention is converted into an irreversible surface that can be read at first light.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding refusal to make an exception removes any reserved portion from the owners' plan. The next ayah answers with an encompassing event. This permits a mimetic reading in which their exceptionless totality returns as total exposure: what they leave outside their planned distribution is also what the event leaves outside its circuit, namely nothing.

activation_trace.role: The encompassing event supplies spatial totality around the target.
Exception as removal from a whole supplies the omitted remainder whose absence makes the owners' plan totalizing.

structural_cues: The negative exception clause in 68:18 immediately precedes the focus event.
The focus repeats the encompassing root as both verb and agent noun.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies no-exception grammar followed by an encompassing pass; I infer a measure-for-measure totality between them. The materially live alternative is simple chronological adjacency with no mimetic arrow.

changed_reading.before: The event happens after a plan that contains no exception.
changed_reading.after: The event can mirror the plan's totality, returning an exceptionless circuit upon those who reserved no exception for anyone else.

context_deltas.mechanism: The encompassing branch can include darkness, the result is named through a branch spanning cut-off night and day, and sight initially yields a claim of being lost. The visitation thus changes more than yield: it carries nocturnal indistinction into morning and erases the target's readable identity or boundaries.

activation_trace.role: Enveloping darkness or event supplies a covering capable of suppressing recognizable features.
Hidden, heedless quiet makes the humans' perceptual absence parallel the target's coming obscurity.
The cut-off night/day image lets nocturnal blackness persist as the material appearance encountered at dawn.
Literal visual recognition supplies the attempted reading of the transformed surface.
Loss of the object explains why seeing first produces disorientation rather than immediate possession.

structural_cues: The owners do not witness the transition and only encounter its completed surface in 68:26.
Their first visual judgment is mislocation or loss before they name deprivation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies darkness, a cut-off night/day image, sight, and loss; I infer that the event erases landscape legibility. The alternative is that the owners merely suppose they took the wrong route while the garden itself remains spatially recognizable.

changed_reading.before: The event removes or ruins the crop while leaving the place conceptually intact.
changed_reading.after: It overwrites the garden's readable surface so thoroughly that the owners first experience the result as loss of place, not merely loss within a place.

context_deltas.mechanism: After the event the owners name themselves with a root that joins crossing a moral limit to the rise of sweeping water. That hydraulic branch resonates with the focus root's enveloping flood or event, allowing the material calamity to externalize their prior overreach as an answering overflow.

activation_trace.role: The enveloping flood or event gives the focus action a hydraulic totality.
Rising, sweeping water makes the owners' confessed overreach materially commensurable with the encompassing event.

structural_cues: The owners apply the overreach root to themselves only after the garden's transformation.
Both activated branches join exceeded bounds to an overwhelming material spread.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies moral overreach and two hydraulic images; I infer that the event materializes the exceeded boundary. A live alternative keeps طغيان metaphorical and the focus event meteorological or agentive without reciprocal correspondence.

changed_reading.before: An external flood-like event overtakes the target.
changed_reading.after: The flood-like totality can be the material counterform of the owners' own overreach, with exceeded moral bounds returning as exceeded physical bounds.

context_deltas.mechanism: The owners respond to the loss by addressing the same Rabb and imagining one thing standing in place of another, directed toward a more beneficial good. Under the corrective-administration baseline, the passing event becomes a threshold between regimes of possession rather than an endpoint consisting only of annihilation.

activation_trace.role: Administration, repair, and completion allow destructive clearing to participate in a longer reordering process.
One thing standing in another's place supplies the post-loss horizon of substitution.
Orientation toward useful good gives the imagined replacement a changed evaluative direction.
The repeated address to the Rabb reconnects hoped-for replacement to the same administering source named in the focus ayah.

structural_cues: The same Rabb relation frames both the nocturnal event and the owners' post-event desire.
The replacement request follows confession rather than preceding the loss.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies loss followed by a Rabb-directed hope for beneficial substitution; I infer that the event can function as a transition in corrective administration. The alternative is that replacement is merely the owners' hope and says nothing about the event's purpose.

changed_reading.after: It can also mark the clearing threshold after which ownership, desire, and good may be reconstituted on another basis.

context_deltas.mechanism: The owners bind themselves by an oath, while the later discourse asks for a writing that establishes judgment and for binding oaths that reach the day of decision. Against that legal field, من ربك and the Rabb branches of authority and covenant let the passing event read as execution of superior jurisdiction over a self-authorized claim.

activation_trace.role: Lordship and ownership provide the superior title under which the event acts.
The covenant and protection-agreement image gives the source phrase a compact juridical resonance.
A distributed binding oath supplies the owners' attempted self-authorization immediately before the event.
Writing that establishes a binding judgment supplies the missing warrant challenged later in the discourse.
The oath branch extends the question of what promise could actually guarantee the claim.
Judgment between claimants supplies the function performed by the superior intervention.

structural_cues: The owners' oath in 68:17 precedes the focus event, while the later questions repeatedly challenge warrants, guarantees, and judgment.
The focus explicitly marks the event as coming from the addressee's Rabb rather than from the owners' plan.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies human oath, superior lordship, covenant imagery, written warrant, binding oath, and judgment; I infer a jurisdictional contest in which the event executes the higher claim. The legal vocabulary may alternatively govern only the later polemic and not the garden event's inner mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The owners' oath is followed by a disaster from a divine source.
changed_reading.after: Their self-binding plan collides with superior title, and the nocturnal pass reads like execution of a judgment their oath could not authorize against the true owner.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later cues combine step-by-step taking, non-recognition, extended time, and concealed strategy. They reopen the apparently punctual طاف: the nocturnal passage can be the terminally visible circuit of a process whose efficacy lies in proceeding while its subjects settle into unknowing security.

activation_trace.role: The incident that comes upon the target supplies the apparently punctual surface event to be temporally revised.
Settling trust turns sleep into the subjective condition that lets an adverse process remain unrecognized.
Taking degree by degree supplies a slow capture mechanism beneath the focus ayah's single completed pass.
Disclosure to a knower, negated in the source construction, makes failed recognition part of the process.
Extended time and respite prevent delay from being mistaken for safety.
Concealed strategy supplies the adverse directional logic joining delay to eventual capture.

structural_cues: The focus compresses the action into a completed nocturnal pass and explicitly foregrounds the subjects' non-awareness through sleep.
The later sequence joins gradual taking to where they do not know and then to deliberate respite.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a punctual pass, trusting sleep, degree-by-degree taking, lack of knowledge, delay, and strategy; I infer that the pass can expose the endpoint of a longer hidden process. The alternative treats the later gradual mechanism as an analogy for other subjects, not as a revision of this event's timing.

changed_reading.before: Everything happens suddenly in one night.
changed_reading.after: The night can be only the moment when a gradual, unrecognized capture closes its circuit and becomes materially undeniable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later companion-of-the-fish sequence moves through circling containment, a blocked outlet, threatened casting into exposed space, and final selection by the Rabb. Read back into the focus, the event is one instance of governance by spatial reassignment: the Rabb can close an estate inside an adverse circuit or bring a contained person through exposure into renewed relation.

activation_trace.role: Circling around a target supplies the focus ayah's enclosing spatial operation.
Administration and corrective tending provide the shared agency behind opposed spatial outcomes.
Circling around water or a thing echoes the focus circuit inside the fish-companion episode.
A stopped outlet after filling supplies the condition of compressed enclosure.
Casting out supplies the abrupt transfer from containment to exposure.
Open unshielded space makes exposure a concrete opposite to the focus event's enclosure.
Selection and drawing near complete a restorative spatial trajectory after threatened exposure.

structural_cues: The later three-ayah sequence repeatedly names the same Rabb who is the stated source of the focus event.
Its movement runs from containment through possible exposure to selection, providing a reversible spatial contrast to the garden's enclosure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two Rabb-centered sequences and opposed enclosure/exposure images; I infer a common mode of governance by spatial reassignment. The alternative keeps the fish-companion episode as an independent exemplum whose rescue should not characterize the garden's destructive pass.

changed_reading.before: The Rabb sends one destructive circuit around an estate.
changed_reading.after: The circuit participates in a broader power to reassign enclosure, exposure, and nearness; the same governance can dispossess a protected space or recover an exposed person.

context_deltas.mechanism: Near the close, hostile sight nearly dislodges a standing person, while hearing the reminder can carry understanding and recovered memory. Against this active sensory field, the sleepers' settled trust is not just lack of wakefulness but loss of perceptual and interpretive grip while the counter-watch operates.

activation_trace.role: The night patrol supplies active surveillance on the event's side.
Settled trust makes sleep a relinquishment of both vigilance and interpretive readiness.
Slipping a thing from its station supplies the threatened loss of stable perceptual footing.
Active eyesight provides the late counterexample to the sleepers' unavailable perception.
Hearing as understanding and compliance shows that sensory contact can become an interpretive response rather than mere reception.
Bringing something back after forgetfulness supplies the recovery that the focus sleepers fail to perform in time.

structural_cues: The focus explicitly opposes an active nocturnal visitor to plural sleepers.
The closing sensory sequence joins seeing, slipping, hearing, and reminder in a single ayah.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies sleep as settled trust and a later field of destabilizing sight plus potentially understanding hearing; I infer that sleep marks epistemic disarmament. The alternative limits وهم نائمون to physical timing with no claim about interpretive posture.

changed_reading.before: Sleep merely explains why the owners do not intervene physically.
changed_reading.after: Sleep also names their loss of perceptual and interpretive grip: the only effective watcher is the visiting patrol, and recognition arrives after stability is gone.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a non-dominant ر ب و mapping and a form-distant cloud branch inside ربك, then couples them to standing water under نائمون. It remains packet-anchored because every image belongs to a supplied branch on a focus word and the split mapping is explicit. Render it only as a material echo or latent weather model, not as a lexical translation of ربك or نائمون.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus alone contains an enveloping-event branch at طاف/طائف, cloud and rising branches under the split mapping of ربك, and a standing-water branch under نائمون.

activation_trace.role: The enveloping flood, rain, or darkness supplies the weather mass that closes around the target.
The low layered cloud supplies a hovering source image within the focus root's dominant inventory.
The non-dominant mapped root's rising and swelling image gives the hovering mass upward and outward pressure.

changed_reading.before: An agentive calamity passes over the target while humans sleep.
changed_reading.after: A latent material model coexists: a rising layered mass envelops the target and settles movement into a standing, water-like stillness.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This reading is surprising because it crosses from physical circling to the running/swimming branch of praise and treats sequence as counter-motion. It remains anchored in the repeated focus root and in the owners' belated تسبيح. Downstream prose should call it a spatial-ritual analogy, not claim that طاف means praise or that the packet states a causal substitution.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The repeated طاف/طائف supplies circling motion, while the context places the owners' call to and performance of تسبيح only after the circuit has completed.

activation_trace.role: Literal circling supplies the nonhuman motion completed around the target.
Running or swimming supplies a second mode of extended motion that can analogically answer the focus circuit.
Worship through praise identifies the human motion or orientation that appears only after the event.

changed_reading.before: The event physically circles the garden and the owners later praise their Rabb.
changed_reading.after: The completed circuit can be heard as a nonhuman counter-motion that precedes and provokes the human ritual orientation the owners had failed to enact.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is odd because it links a night patrol to context images of covert speech and movement, making the event an inverse circulation of secrecy. It remains valid as a focus-anchored social analogy: the event patrols while sleepers are hidden, and the owners later move in whispers. Render it as a contrast in circulation and disclosure, not as personification of literal gossip.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The night-patrol branch at طائف and heedless hiddenness at نائمون permit comparison with the owners' later covert movement and speech.

activation_trace.role: The night patrol supplies a quiet circulation that observes or acts while others are inactive.
Hidden heedlessness supplies the sleepers' unobservant social posture.
A covert sound or movement that reveals its source supplies the paradox that secrecy itself leaves evidence.
Lowered secret speech supplies the owners' own quiet circulation after the event has already acted.

changed_reading.before: The event is silent because it occurs during sleep, and the owners later whisper for privacy.
changed_reading.after: Two covert circulations oppose one another: the owners whisper to hide exclusion, while the counter-patrol has already moved silently enough to expose what their secrecy protects.

strongest_changes: The pass became a counter-boundary that reverses planned exclusion into the owners' own deprivation.
The event became a timed assay by severance, turning hidden intention into a dawn-readable result.
Later gradual-taking cues reopened the apparently sudden night as the visible closure of a longer unrecognized process.
Repeated Rabb-centered enclosure and exposure sequences made the event one mode of corrective spatial governance rather than ownerless weather.
summary.what_was_special: The verb-agent doubling of ط و ف kept several mechanisms live at once: encompassing event, visiting incident, adverse night patrol, hydraulic spread, and bounded circuit. Context did not collapse them; it redirected them into social reversal, assay, jurisdiction, perceptual erasure, gradual capture, and restorative or destructive spatial reassignment.
remaining_uncertainties: The ayah does not force a choice among agentive patrol, enveloping event, and weather-like material process.
The reciprocal, legal, and ritual models may describe deliberate causal structure or may remain sequence-based analogies.
The rising-cloud-standing-water model depends on intentionally form-distant branches, including the packet's non-dominant ر ب و mapping, and should remain exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **An encompassing event reverses enclosure.** The verb and noun repeat `ط و ف B002`, an enveloping flood, darkness, or event, around the garden; `ر ب ب B001/B002` supplies authoritative nurture. The garden had enclosed its produce (`ج ن ن B003`), but now an event encompasses the enclosure. I infer that a higher governing circuit overrides the owners' bounded control; the ayah reverses who or what surrounds whom.
2. **A visiting incident during misplaced security.** `ط و ف B003` supplies a visiting apparition or incident, while `ن و م B001/B005` supplies sleep and settled trust. The simultaneous clause contrasts active visitation with passive sleepers. I infer trust in continuity -> lowered vigilance; the event reads as arriving precisely through the temporal gap their confidence leaves unguarded.
3. **Stillness hiding decisive motion.** `ن و م B004/B009` adds obscurity, heedless quiet, and stillness after motion. The packet gives no described human witness to the event. I infer that absence of perceived motion does not mean absence of effective change; the ayah makes sleep a model of epistemic concealment, later answered by sight in 68:26.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 68:44-45 unexpectedly generalize this night visitation into gradual action from an unknown point under extended time. The sleepers become an early concrete model of people inhabiting a decisive process without perceiving it.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A counter-patrol during false security.** Fixed `طَافَ / طَائِف` activates `ط و ف B005` (night patrol), while fixed `نَائِمُون` activates `ن و م B005` (settling trust or feeling secure). Their oath in 68:17 and absent contingency in 68:18 supply confident possession; I infer that settled trust disables their watch and is answered by a patrol from outside their control. The event reads as a reversal of surveillance: the owners sleep while their garden is inspected and acted upon.
2. **Lordly nurture operating through an encompassing event.** Fixed `طَائِف` also activates `ط و ف B002` (an enveloping flood, darkness, or event), and fixed `رَبِّكَ` activates `ر ب ب B002` (repair and nurture). The blackened result in 68:20 and the later recognition sequence supply destruction followed by moral correction; I infer that the encompassing event blocks exploitative use and thereby enables repair of the agents. Lordship here reads as corrective cultivation through loss, while the destructive → corrective arrow remains my abduction.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 68:20-24 revealed that the nocturnal event does more than destroy: it begins a chain that exposes exclusionary purpose. That later disclosure made fixed `رَبِّكَ` activate corrective nurture (`ر ب ب B002`) through the encompassing visitor, while fixed sleep became misplaced security (`ن و م B005`).

baseline.text: Onlar uyurken Rabbin tarafından gelen bir felaket bahçeyi sarıp geçti.

findings.text: Bahçeyi kuşatan olay, sahiplerin çevreleyip denetlediği mülkün bu kez daha üstün bir yönetim tarafından çevrelenmesini sağlar.
Sahiplerin güven içinde uyuması ile gece devriyesi gibi gelen olay karşı karşıya getirilir; gözetlediklerini sananlar gözetimsiz yakalanır.
Yıkıcı olayın daha sonra itiraf ve yöneliş doğurması, Rabbin bakımının kayıp yoluyla da düzeltici biçimde işleyebildiğini gösterir.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] The Orchard Moves from Assay to Cultivation, Cutting, and Meal
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Productive value is disclosed through a staged cycle: weathering and test, prepared soil, ripened growth, harvest, and consumption.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The owners are themselves processed like the orchard: wear and testing reveal condition, while planning, cutting, and morning consumption specify the material sequence they try to control.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Soil Is Prepared and Growth Is Tended
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Seed enters worked ground, cultivation compacts a route through the field, and sheltered vegetation rises toward fruiting.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: tree-covered orchard (`quranic:root_000266:B003/m02`); dense rising vegetation (`quranic:root_000266:B011/m02`); earning through labor (`quranic:root_000303:B001/m01`); casting seed into prepared soil (`quranic:root_000303:B002/m01`); worked or trampled field (`quranic:root_000303:B008/m01`); tending and completion (`quranic:root_000532:B002/m03`); persistent green plant (`quranic:root_000532:B012/m02`); pollinating tall palms (`quranic:root_000946:B014/m01`); palm cluster and dates (`quranic:root_001015:B005/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The orchard is a managed system rather than an undifferentiated abundance. Soil preparation, seed, compacted access, tending, palm pollination, and fruit cluster each occupy a different role in production.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Water and Milk Must Keep Moving Through a Managed Circuit
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A living resource remains productive only when rain, stored water, pasture, herd movement, and milk transfer continue through connected stages.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The garden’s loss is reframed as a broken hydrological and husbandry circuit: dew, trough, repeated watering, pasture, lactation, and access can each be the point of arrest.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Rain, Dew, Flood, and Deep Water Form the Supply
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Cloud and dew wet the land, an encircling flood enlarges the flow, and water collects in a deep store that may be sweet and usable.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: rain cloud (`quranic:root_000532:B008/m02`); abundant collected water (`quranic:root_000532:B013/m03`); dew and rain (`quranic:root_001486:B003/m01`); moisture and wet ground (`quranic:root_001487:B005/m01`); surrounding flood (`quranic:root_000957:B002/m01`); wetness retained in a skin (`quranic:root_000152:B001/m01`); deep well or sea (`quranic:root_001040:B005/m02`); sweet potable water (`quranic:root_000994:B001/m01`).

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The supply is assembled across atmospheric, surface, and stored water. The “sweetness” branch of `ع ذ ب` provides a sharp latent reversal: the verse’s punishment stands lexically beside the desirable water whose loss makes deprivation tangible.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Water and Milk Must Keep Moving Through a Managed Circuit
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A living resource remains productive only when rain, stored water, pasture, herd movement, and milk transfer continue through connected stages.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The garden’s loss is reframed as a broken hydrological and husbandry circuit: dew, trough, repeated watering, pasture, lactation, and access can each be the point of arrest.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Herds Cycle Between Trough, Pasture, and Return
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Animals leave the watering place, graze nearby, return for another drink, and are held within a managed rhythm of release and rest.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: cycling herd between water and pasture (`quranic:root_001486:B006/m01`); repeated watering circuit (`quranic:root_001487:B004/m01`); re-entry to the trough (`quranic:root_000464:B007/m01`); watering at the animals’ mouths (`quranic:root_001198:B014/m01`); camels released to graze and drink (`quranic:root_000946:B006/m01`); camel that remains at its morning resting-place (`quranic:root_000839:B008/m01`); herd (`quranic:root_000532:B014/m03`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:19 `رَّبِّ` [ر ب ب]; 68:20/21 `أَصْبَحَتْ`/`مُصْبِحِينَ` [ص ب ح]; 68:21 `تَنَادَ` [ن د و]; 68:23 `ٱنطَلَقُ` [ط ل ق]; 68:24 `يَدْخُلَ` [د خ ل]; 68:30 `أَقْبَلَ` [ق ب ل]; surface anchor unavailable for root `ن د ي`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Husbandry depends on regulated recurrence rather than one act of watering. Release, mouth-level watering, nearby grazing, re-entry, and morning rest define a complete circuit whose interruption produces loss without requiring the animal itself to disappear.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] An Unseen Night Passage Produces a Visible Morning State
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Concealment and stillness permit an event to pass around its target, after which morning makes the transformed condition visible.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The nocturnal event combines watch, encirclement, flood, dreamless stillness, blackening, and visual recognition into a temporal mechanism rather than a bare calamity.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Garden, Night, and Sleep Layer Concealment
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Trees enclose the garden, night covers it, and sleeping occupants become still, trusting, and inattentive.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: sensory cover (`quranic:root_000266:B001/m02`); night covering in blackness (`quranic:root_000266:B002/m01`); enclosed garden (`quranic:root_000266:B003/m03`); sleep (`quranic:root_001568:B001/m01`); obscurity and heedlessness (`quranic:root_001568:B004/m01`); restful trust (`quranic:root_001568:B005/m01`); sleeping after dawn (`quranic:root_000839:B007/m01`); voice extinguished into deathlike silence (`quranic:root_000425:B002/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Four covers coincide: vegetation, darkness, sleep, and silence. Their joint effect is not guilt by association but scene construction: the owners cannot observe or answer the event while it acts.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] An Unseen Night Passage Produces a Visible Morning State
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Concealment and stillness permit an event to pass around its target, after which morning makes the transformed condition visible.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The nocturnal event combines watch, encirclement, flood, dreamless stillness, blackening, and visual recognition into a temporal mechanism rather than a bare calamity.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Visitor Circles as Event, Watch, and Enclosure
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Something approaches and circles the orchard like a patrol or enclosing flood, traversing its perimeter while its occupants remain still.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: circling around a target (`quranic:root_000957:B001/m01`); encompassing flood or incident (`quranic:root_000957:B002/m02`); approaching apparition or event (`quranic:root_000957:B003/m01`); night watchman (`quranic:root_000957:B005/m01`); defensive perimeter wall (`quranic:root_000957:B010/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The visitor’s operation is spatially exact: approach, circuit, enclosure. The watchman sense reverses the expected function of patrol, since what circles under divine commission does not preserve the owners’ property regime.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Boundary Operations Decide What Remains Inside the Whole
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Folding, exception, enclosure, entry, binding, and release all alter membership in a bounded whole.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The exclusion of the poor is represented as a general boundary technology: a whole can be folded, have a portion excepted, be walled, or be opened by release.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Folding and Exception Remove a Portion from the Whole
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: One item is doubled, repeated, folded back, or explicitly removed from the rule governing the surrounding set.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: joining a second to a first (`quranic:root_000208:B001/m01`); repeated operation (`quranic:root_000208:B003/m01`); folding or turning aside (`quranic:root_000208:B005/m01`); exception from a general rule (`quranic:root_000208:B008/m01`); allotted portion (`quranic:root_001226:B003/m02`); part opposed to whole (`quranic:root_000133:B001/m01`); group or piece (`quranic:root_000957:B004/m01`); cut portion (`quranic:root_000861:B005/m02`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Exception is materially modeled by the fold: a portion is turned out of the common line and separately treated. The repeated, doubled, allotted, and cut senses distinguish several operations that can produce an excluded part.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Collective identity changes as speech moves from summons and secrecy to confrontation, mediation, confession, and blame.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Speech does not merely narrate the owners’ change; its forms reorganize them from a coordinated bloc into facing parts with a middle voice and shared admission.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: A Cohesive Group Fragments into Portions
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A formerly assembled body scatters, becomes factions or isolated pieces, and loses the prestige that held it together.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: people scattered in directions (`quranic:root_000153:B009/m01`); dispersal and disarray (`quranic:root_000154:B008/m01`); cut-off tract or group (`quranic:root_000861:B005/m03`); faction or fragment (`quranic:root_000957:B004/m02`); divided attention (`quranic:root_001226:B006/m01`); fall of inherited status (`quranic:root_001281:B005/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:17 `بَلَوْ` [ب ل و], `أَقْسَمُ` [ق س م], and `يَصْرِمُ` [ص ر م]; 68:19 `طَآئِفٌ` [ط و ف]; 68:33 `أَكْبَرُ` [ك ب ر]; surface anchor unavailable for root `ب ل ي`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Fragmentation is the social analogue of harvest-cutting. The group that jointly planned exclusion is itself rendered into scattered portions, with status no longer functioning as cohesion.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Intention becomes effective only when plan, capacity, route, bodily movement, and recognition remain aligned.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The owners’ confident departure is anatomized into distinct failure points: crooked gait, wrong direction, insufficient capacity, or a seeing that cannot identify its own destination.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Intent Is Calculated Before the Body Moves
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A goal is selected, deliberated, measured against capacity, and converted into an operational plan.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: directed intent and effort (`quranic:root_000305:B001/m01`); anger energizing intent (`quranic:root_000305:B003/m01`); reflective judgment (`quranic:root_000531:B002/m01`); ability and possession (`quranic:root_001205:B003/m01`); planning by measure (`quranic:root_001205:B005/m02`); proportioned fit (`quranic:root_001205:B006/m01`); divided deliberation (`quranic:root_001226:B006/m02`); cultivated knowledge (`quranic:root_000532:B003/m02`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Purpose is not identical with capacity. Anger can intensify intention, but deliberation, proportion, knowledge, and actual ability must still agree before the plan can reach its object.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Oaths Allocate Risk, Exception, and Protection
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A spoken commitment binds parties only through its scope, reservation, guarantor, and protected rights.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The owners’ oath is lexically surrounded by legal mechanisms that they suppress: exception, distributed liability, truce, surety, companionship, and inviolable claim.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Treaty, Surety, and Companionship Carry Protected Rights
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Truce restrains conflict, a surety bears liability, covenant defines inviolable rights, and a companion preserves the person under care.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: truce (`quranic:root_001226:B008/m01`); protected time without fighting (`quranic:root_000313:B005/m01`); inviolable right and guarantee (`quranic:root_000313:B006/m02`); surety and written undertaking (`quranic:root_001198:B008/m01`); covenant (`quranic:root_000532:B011/m02`); companionship and charge (`quranic:root_000844:B001/m01`); preservation through companionship (`quranic:root_000844:B002/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:17 `أَصْحَٰبَ` [ص ح ب] and `أَقْسَمُ` [ق س م]; 68:19/29/32 forms of `ر ب ب` [ر ب ب]; 68:27 `مَحْرُومُونَ` [ح ر م]; 68:30 `أَقْبَلَ` [ق ب ل].
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Obligation distributes vulnerability. Truce protects time, covenant protects relation, surety carries another’s burden, and companionship protects a person; the owners’ compact instead concentrates protection inside their own group.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Loss Reorients Desire Toward Replacement and Repair
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: After deprivation, hope becomes a directed search for a substitute that restores function and exceeds the lost provision.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Replacement is not a reset: it can change only outward form, occupy another’s place, restore a depleted flow, or answer desire with a more generous provision.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Substitution and Repair Restore a Failed Function
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: One thing takes another’s place or changes form; tending and recovery seek to make the replacement function better than what failed.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: substitute occupying another’s place (`quranic:root_000095:B001/m01`); changed form (`quranic:root_000095:B002/m01`); gradual repair (`quranic:root_000532:B002/m04`); recovery after wasting (`quranic:root_000152:B003/m02`); selection of the better option (`quranic:root_000452:B003/m01`); compatibility through association (`quranic:root_000844:B004/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:17 `أَصْحَٰبَ` [ص ح ب]; 68:19/29/32 forms of `ر ب ب` [ر ب ب]; 68:32 `يُبْدِلَ` [ب د ل] and `خَيْرًا` [خ ي ر]; surface anchor unavailable for root `ب ل ل`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Replacement has two distinct operations: exchange the occupant, or transform the existing form. Repair and compatibility then test whether the new arrangement truly restores the broken function.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Folding and Joining Build Portable or Fixed Enclosures
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Boundaries are made by folding flexible material, fastening parts, or raising a perimeter around a protected interior.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Logical exception and property exclusion share a craft image: a fold or wall redirects a portion away from common access.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Folded Cloth and Palm Fiber Make a Container
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Cloth is folded, doubled with cord, cut into a piece, and joined to palm fiber or straps to hold a harvest.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: fold of cloth or book (`quranic:root_000208:B005/m02`); doubled-ended rope (`quranic:root_000208:B007/m01`); first fold of cloth (`quranic:root_001226:B007/m01`); cloth-piece (`quranic:root_000957:B004/m03`); woven palm basket (`quranic:root_000464:B010/m02`); joined straps and patches (`quranic:root_001198:B010/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The portable enclosure is assembled through operations, not motifs piled by topic: fold, double, cut, weave, and join. It converts a flat surface into a volume capable of holding produce.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Folding and Joining Build Portable or Fixed Enclosures
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Boundaries are made by folding flexible material, fastening parts, or raising a perimeter around a protected interior.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Logical exception and property exclusion share a craft image: a fold or wall redirects a portion away from common access.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Wall, Sanctuary, and Raft Define an Interior by Perimeter
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A wall circles a place, sacred rights thicken its boundary, and lashed timbers can carry a bounded platform over water.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: perimeter wall (`quranic:root_000957:B010/m02`); circling a bounded place (`quranic:root_000957:B001/m02`); lashed raft (`quranic:root_000957:B006/m01`); sanctuary and surrounding rights (`quranic:root_000313:B003/m02`); interior entry (`quranic:root_000464:B001/m02`); rudder stabilizing a vessel (`quranic:root_000726:B008/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:19 `طَافَ`/`طَآئِفٌ` [ط و ف]; 68:24 `يَدْخُلَ` [د خ ل] and `مِّسْكِينٌ` [س ك ن]; 68:27 `مَحْرُومُونَ` [ح ر م].
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Fixed wall and floating raft share a perimeter principle: joined material produces a stable inside despite pressure from outside. Sanctuary adds the social right that makes such a boundary more than construction.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Worship Redirects Blame into Redress and Giving
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Corrective speech exonerates the giver, acknowledges wrong, and restores outward movement through worship, acceptance, and generosity.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Praise is not isolated ritual language; it changes the social direction of goods by replacing exclusion and self-justification with accepted fault, protected relation, and largesse.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Generosity Reopens the Arrested Flow
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Good deed, recovery, gift, and largesse move provision outward after deprivation has exposed the harm of enclosure.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: excellent benefaction (`quranic:root_000153:B003/m01`); witnessed good deed (`quranic:root_000154:B003/m01`); recovery and welfare (`quranic:root_000152:B003/m03`); generosity (`quranic:root_000452:B005/m03`); abundant gift (`quranic:root_000575:B004/m02`); gracious provision (`quranic:root_000532:B016/m03`); noble character (`quranic:root_000994:B008/m01`); dew-like giving (`quranic:root_001486:B004/m01`); generous hand (`quranic:root_001487:B008/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:17 `بَلَوْ` [ب ل و]; 68:19/29/32 forms of `ر ب ب` [ر ب ب]; 68:21 `تَنَادَ` [ن د و]; 68:32 `خَيْرًا` [خ ي ر] and `رَٰغِبُونَ` [ر غ ب]; 68:33 `عَذَابُ` [ع ذ ب]; surface anchors unavailable for roots `ب ل ي`, `ب ل ل`, and `ن د ي`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Generosity is the inverse of the owners’ plan at the level of flow. It converts possession into outward provision, while good deed and recovery show that giving can restore both social relation and material condition.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Life-Cycle Thresholds Can Be Nurtured or Arrested
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Birth, maturation, lactation, and death are thresholds whose continuation depends on care, release, and supply.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The threatened orchard is mirrored by animal and human life cycles: fetus, labor, midwife, milk, grave, and death each show growth either brought through a threshold or deliberately stopped.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Fetus, Labor, and Reception at Birth
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A concealed fetus reaches labor, the body opens under pain, and an attendant receives the newborn into social care.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: fetus hidden in the womb (`quranic:root_000266:B007/m01`); dependent child under care (`quranic:root_000532:B005/m01`); labor pain (`quranic:root_000946:B008/m01`); abdominal release (`quranic:root_000946:B009/m01`); inner bodily channels (`quranic:root_000946:B017/m01`); afterbirth and womb (`quranic:root_000994:B009/m01`); unborn livestock (`quranic:root_001076:B005/m01`); midwife receiving the child (`quranic:root_001198:B007/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Birth is a multi-role transition: concealed occupant, laboring body, opening passage, expelled afterbirth, and receiving attendant. It gives precise biological content to the pericope’s concern with whether a hoped-for yield reaches completion.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 68:17-33] Life-Cycle Thresholds Can Be Nurtured or Arrested
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Birth, maturation, lactation, and death are thresholds whose continuation depends on care, release, and supply.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The threatened orchard is mirrored by animal and human life cycles: fetus, labor, midwife, milk, grave, and death each show growth either brought through a threshold or deliberately stopped.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Grave-Camel Makes Arrested Care Visible
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A camel is tied at its owner’s grave, denied food and water until death, while related senses register stopped milk, immobility, and the end of productive life.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: grave-camel left to die (`quranic:root_000153:B005/m01`); tethered burial animal (`quranic:root_000154:B006/m01`); milk and rain stopped (`quranic:root_000305:B005/m02`); camel remaining down at morning (`quranic:root_000839:B008/m02`); grazing camel otherwise released (`quranic:root_000946:B006/m02`); death or killing figured as sleep (`quranic:root_001568:B008/m01`); burial cover (`quranic:root_000266:B009/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 68:17 `بَلَوْ` [ب ل و] and `جَنَّةِ` [ج ن ن]; 68:17/20/21 forms of `ص ب ح` [ص ب ح]; 68:19 `نَآئِمُونَ` [ن و م]; 68:23 `ٱنطَلَقُ` [ط ل ق]; 68:25 `حَرْدٍ` [ح ر د]; surface anchor unavailable for root `ب ل ي`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The grave-camel is a complete counter-husbandry scene: binding replaces release, fasting replaces pasture, and death replaces yield. It intensifies the orchard narrative’s exposure of possession severed from sustaining care.
